scores.evidence: Three can-do objectives (o1 and o3 「説明できる」, o2 「見分けて、AIへの依頼を書き分けられる」) each have 2+ questions with objectiveId and an apply item: o1 q1, q6; o2 q2, q9, q5; o3 q7, q8, q4, q3. The exam check-quiz covers all three with transfer contexts (q6 美容院の予約アプリ, q5 家計簿アプリ, q3 友人の助言).

hook-b1 sets a concrete problem in three sentences (「ページを再読み込みすると、入力したタスクが消えてしまいます」) that s1-b4 and the 1-5 example come back to, then the predict q0. q0's options are not parallel: b (29 characters, the only one about saving, naming バックエンド and データベース before 1-1 defines them) stands out against a (19) and c (15), and no option has feedback.

The ch0 prerequisite is stated and recalled in s1-b1 (「人間は「何を作るか」を示し、正しいかを判断する役だと確認しました」), every defined term follows an everyday analogy that says what maps to what (s1-b3, s2-analogy, s3-analogy, s4-analogy), and the glossary matches the definitions. The hook already uses バックエンド and データベース (q0 option b and its explanation) before s1-b5 defines them.

measure.mjs counts 2,392 of the 2,400 prose characters, lint finds no sentence, paragraph, callout or list overrun, and no segment defines more than 3 terms. Section 1-2 is crowded for one segment: 3 new terms, a JSON code block, a tip, two prompt examples, a quiz and askTutor (10 blocks).

ex-steps shows 6 subgoal-labelled steps (「① 足りないものを書き出す」 … 「⑥ 再読み込みして確かめる」) with the reason in ①–④, an expect on each and a troubleshoot on ⑥; q9 then fades one step and the practice transfers the procedure to a reading-log app. Step ⑤ (ex-screen) gives no reason, and the faded item q9 asks for the 「最初に送る依頼」 although step ③ makes the commit the first request.

Every content section has an inline check with feedback on each wrong option, but the keyed option is the longest (or tied) in all 10 questions and 8 of 10 keys are option ②, exam items q6, q5 and q4 included; the reader numbers options by position and never shuffles, so 'pick the longest, usually ②' answers nearly every item. q7 restates s3-b1 (「自分のパソコンでアプリが動いても、そのままでは、ほかの人は使えません」), and q9's stem contradicts step ③.

The brief's four misconceptions are each corrected with a reason, in feedback of at most 2 sentences: unsaved data lost on reload (hook-predict, s1-b4, q6), looks vs data (s2-b5, q2, q5, q9 a), local or built is not public (q7 a and c, q4 a), and rewind or commit-after instead of commit-first (s4-tools, q3 a and b, q8 c). Some distractors tempt few learners (q0 c 「ブラウザのバージョンが古いから」, q6 d 「別のブラウザ」, q4 d 「データベースの記録が、すべて新しくなった」), and q3's feedback overstates what AI rewind features are.

The one diagram s1-b2 shows the structure in 4 nodes whose labels match the text's terms in both locales, with a caption that states the takeaway (「ユーザーが触るのはフロントエンドだけ。データの出し入れは、バックエンドとデータベースがおこなう」), alt text and a description. The three deploy steps are a numbered list (s3-b2), and there are no decorative images.

practice-task sets a transfer task (読書記録アプリ, three requests, about 5 minutes) with a 5-item checklist and two model answers, so success is stated. But practice-answer-ui only shows the date (「本の一覧に、APIから受け取った「読み終えた日」を表示してください」), so the modelled requests give no way to enter it, and both hints sit in one always-visible callout (practice-hint).

After the exam come 4 summary points, a reflection and next step (summary-next), 7 flashcards and askTutor. The o2 takeaway and its card, though, tell the learner to ask the UI or the API (「見た目を変えたいならUI、届くデータを変えたいならAPIに頼みます」; EN 'Ask the UI for changes in looks'), not to ask the AI for a UI or API change.

Claims trace to sources recorded in the brief and facts (checkedAt 2026-10-30, Git 2.56 pinned), the original's unsupported claims were dropped, and s4-b4 keeps Pro Git's hedge (「ほぼ必ず戻れます」). But q3 states for every AI tool what only Claude Code's checkpointing page says (「巻き戻しはその場の作業を戻すためのもので、Gitの代わりではありません」), and its option d feedback asserts AI behaviour no source gives (「AIの答えを変えるものではありません」).

です・ます throughout, warm and pressure-free (「まず予想してみましょう」「安心して試せます」), and lint finds no banned phrase. A few stiff or shifting spots: 「ファイルを小さくした、サーバーに送れる一式ができます」 (s3-defs), 「デプロイの3つの流れは？」 (cards), and 「ホール」 in s2-analogy where s1-b3 said 「客席とウェイター」.

Every learner-facing text, diagram labels and alt included, is in jp and en (lint locale-plain-string is clean), and there are no images or links. The EN drifts in places: summary-points 'Ask the UI for changes in looks' misstates the action, s2-b5 says 'Some AI tools' official guides' for the one guide cited, and ex-lead adds 'using what you have learned so far'.

mustFix.issue: Answer cues: in all 10 questions the keyed option is the longest or tied (characters: q0 29 vs 19/15, q1 23 vs ≤19, q2 24 vs ≤20, q9 31 vs 24, q6 20 vs ≤18, q5 40 vs ≤28, q4 26 vs ≤20, q3 30 vs ≤26; q7 ties, q8 leads by 1), and 8 of 10 keys are option ② (q0, q1, q7, q8, q9, q6, q5, q4). QuizCheckBlock numbers options by position and never shuffles, so 'the longest, usually ②' answers the inline checks and three of the four graded exam items without the knowledge; contract §4 asks for options parallel in length.
mustFix.fix: (1) Reorder the options arrays, keeping every option id and answer: s1-check q1 [a, c, d, b]; s3-check q7 [b, a, c, d]; s4-check q8 [a, c, d, b]; ex-check q9 [a, c, b, d]; check-quiz q6 [a, c, d, b], q5 [b, a, c, d], q4 [a, c, b, d], q3 [a, c, b, d]. The keys then sit at ④ ③ ① ④ ③ for q1, q2, q7, q8, q9 and ④ ① ③ ② for q6, q5, q4, q3. (2) Make each key no longer than its longest distractor, by shortening the key or giving a distractor a plausible clause, largest gaps first: q5 b → 「金額を右寄せで少し大きくして。APIとデータベースは変えないで」 and q5 c → 「金額を返すAPIを作り直して、一覧の金額も右寄せで大きくして」; q9 a → 「タスク一覧の各タスクに、期限の日付を表示して。APIは変えないで」 (its feedback still holds); then q4, q2, q1 and q3. Keep the EN in step.

mustFix.issue: q9 asks for the 「最初に送る依頼」 and keys the data-side request b, but step ③ of the worked example (「頼む前にコミットする」) and the practice checklist item pc-commit (「最初の依頼で、いまの状態のコミットを頼んでいる」) make the commit the first request, and no option is a commit. Right before the practice, the item teaches the opposite of the commit-first habit.
mustFix.fix: State that the commit is done and ask for the next request. JP prompt: 「直ったタスク管理アプリに「期限」を足して、再読み込みしても残るようにしたいとします。いまの状態のコミットは済ませました。次に送る依頼として、最も適切なのはどれでしょう？」 EN: 'You want to add due dates to the fixed task app and keep them after a reload. You have already committed the current state. Which request should you send next?'

mustFix.issue: The task is to record 「読み終えた日」 for each book and show it (practice-task), but the model answers never let the learner enter it: practice-answer-data makes it storable and returned, and practice-answer-ui only displays it (「本の一覧に、APIから受け取った「読み終えた日」を表示してください」). The modelled requests produce a column nobody can fill, the checklist does not catch the omission, and the worked example's step ⑤ did ask for 「追加もAPIで保存して」.
mustFix.fix: practice-answer-ui prompt JP → 「本ごとに「読み終えた日」を入力できるようにして、APIで保存してください。本の一覧には、APIから受け取った読み終えた日を表示してください。APIとデータベースは変更しないでください。」, EN → 'Let me enter the date finished for each book and save it through the API. Show the date finished received from the API in the book list. Do not change the API or the database.'; expect JP → 「読み終えた日を入力でき、一覧の各本に表示されます。再読み込みしても残ります。」, EN → 'You can enter the date finished, and each book in the list shows it. It is still there after a reload.' Add to practice-checklist an item pc-input: 「画面側の依頼に、読み終えた日を入力してAPIで保存することが書いてある」 / 'The screen-side request lets you enter the date and save it through the API'.

mustFix.issue: q3 states as a fact about every AI tool what the cited page (cc-checkpointing) says only of Claude Code: option a's feedback 「巻き戻しはその場の作業を戻すためのもので、Gitの代わりではありません。」 and the explanation 「AIツールの巻き戻しは、Gitの代わりではありません。」. The brief keeps this claim to Claude Code, as s4-tools does (「たとえばAIツールのClaude Codeも…」). Option d's feedback 「コミットは状態を記録するだけで、AIの答えを変えるものではありません。」 asserts AI behaviour that no source gives.
mustFix.fix: Option a feedback JP → 「巻き戻しが、Gitの代わりになるとは限りません。たとえばClaude Codeの公式ドキュメントは、代わりではないと書いています。」, EN → 'A rewind feature does not necessarily replace Git. Claude Code's official documentation, for example, says its rewind does not.'; explanation JP → 「コミットした状態には、あとからほぼ必ず戻れます。AIツールの巻き戻しが、Gitの代わりになるとは限りません。頼む前に、動いている状態をコミットしておきます。」, EN → 'You can almost always get back to a committed state, and an AI tool's rewind does not necessarily replace Git. Commit the working state before you ask.'; option d feedback JP → 「コミットは状態を記録するもので、AIの間違いを防ぐ仕組みではありません。間違えたときに戻る場所を作るために使います。」, EN → 'A commit records a state; it is not a way to prevent AI mistakes. It gives you a place to return to when something goes wrong.'

mustFix.issue: The o2 takeaway tells the learner to ask the UI or the API: 「見た目を変えたいならUI、届くデータを変えたいならAPIに頼みます。」 (EN 'Ask the UI for changes in looks and the API for changes in the data that arrives'), repeated by card card-ui-api in the cards block (「それぞれどこに頼む？」 → 「…APIに頼みます」). The lesson defines the API as the window through which the frontend asks the backend for data (s2-b2), so asking the API is what the frontend does; the learner asks the AI for a UI change or an API change, as q2 puts it (「AIに「APIが返すデータを変えて」と頼む」).
mustFix.fix: summary-points item 2 JP → 「見た目はUIの変更、届くデータはAPIの変更として、AIに頼みます。依頼には、変えない範囲も書きます。」 (same length, so prose stays within 2,400), EN → 'Ask the AI for a UI change when you want different looks, and for an API change when you want different data. Say what should not change, too.'; in cards, card-ui-api front JP → 「見た目を変えたいとき、届くデータを変えたいとき、それぞれ何の変更としてAIに頼む？」, back → 「見た目はUIの変更、届くデータはAPIの変更として頼みます。」, EN front → 'When you want different looks, or different data, what kind of change do you ask the AI for?', back → 'Looks: a UI change. The data that arrives: an API change.'

niceToHave: hook-predict q0: make the options parallel and keep undefined terms out: b → 「データを保存する仕組みがないから」 (EN 'Nothing saves the data'), and give a and c feedback as vibe-ch2's hook does (the reader shows the picked option's feedback after a prediction): a → 「画面が完成していても、保存する仕組みがなければ、再読み込みでデータは消えます。」, c → 「ブラウザが新しくても、保存していないデータは再読み込みで消えます。」

practice-hint shows both hints at once, before the attempt, and Hint 2 hands over the data-side request. lesson-schema-get returns this practice section as the exemplar, so use the folded hints the contract names, as vibe-ch2-practice does: a steps block (p-commit, p-data, p-screen, each with expect) with Hint 1 as p-data.hint and Hint 2 as p-data.troubleshoot, cited like ex-steps, plus an explicit hint for the screen side, e.g. 「1-5の⑤の依頼の「追加もAPIで保存して」を、読み終えた日に置きかえます」.

s3-analogy and q4 assume the build runs on your own computer before the transfer (「自宅の台所…下ごしらえがビルド」, q4's key 「まだサーバーにはない」), while mdn-publishing as the facts record it describes hosts that fetch the source from GitHub and build it, the flow ch8 teaches (「コードをpushするたびに自動でサイトが更新されます」). Say where the build ran in q4: 「自分のパソコンで、ビルドが終わりました。この時点の説明として、正しいのはどれでしょう？」, and keep s3-flow length-neutral: 「[[デプロイ]]は、大きく次の3つに分かれます。」
No question tests the launch step (起動), and q7 restates s3-b1; q7 could ask what is still missing once the files are on the server and nobody can open the app yet (key: 起動), leaving q4 for the build.

q6: replace d (「利用者に、別のブラウザを使ってもらう」), which tempts few learners, with the UI-only fix of the brief's misconception 2, e.g. 「予約画面で、満席の時間を選べないようにするだけにする」 with feedback 「画面で選べなくしても、届いた予約を受け付けるかどうかは、バックエンドが決めます。そこの確認を直します。」
When rebalancing lengths, also reword q1's key, which echoes the backend definition (「届いた金額を確かめて」 vs s1-b5 「届いたデータや依頼を確かめ」), e.g. 「入力された金額を調べてから、保存させる」.
s2-analogy: 「ホールが決まった頼み方で」 → 「ウェイターが決まった頼み方で」, so it keeps s1-b3's mapping (客席とウェイター＝フロントエンド).

s3-analogy puts the restaurant on the server side (「お店（サーバー）」) right after 1-1 and 1-2 made its dining room the frontend in the browser, and 「下ごしらえ」 (prep before cooking) fits packaging finished code loosely; consider 「持ち運べるように詰め直すのがビルド（build）」 or a scene outside the restaurant, trimming elsewhere to stay within the prose budget (2,392 of 2,400).
ex-screen (step ⑤) is the only step without a reason; add one, e.g. 「APIができたので、画面はそれを使うだけにします。」, and trim the same number of characters elsewhere.

ex-verify troubleshoot names one cause; saving or loading can miss the API: 「消えてしまうときは、保存か読み込みのどちらかが、APIを通っていません。⑤の依頼を見直して、頼み直します。」 (EN 'If it disappears, either saving or loading is not going through the API. Check the request in step 5 and ask again.')
q9 explanation: 「表示は、そのあとで頼みます。」 → 「入力と表示は、そのあとで画面側に頼みます。」 (EN 'Ask the screen side for the input and the display after that.'), to match ex-screen.

s2-b5 EN: 'Some AI tools' official guides say the AI keeps to the scope you state.' → 'One AI tool's official guide says the AI keeps to the scope you state.' Only cc-champion-kit is cited; the JP 「公式ガイドもあります」 is fine.
s3-defs and glossary: 「ファイルを小さくした、サーバーに送れる一式ができます。」 → 「小さくまとめた、サーバーに送れるファイル一式ができます。」; cards card-deploy front: 「デプロイの3つの流れは？」 → 「デプロイの3つの段階は？」.
ex-lead EN adds 'using what you have learned so far', which the JP does not say; drop it, or add 「ここまでの内容を使って、」 to the JP.
summary: The lesson's spine is strong: the hook's vanishing tasks are explained in 1-1, fixed in a subgoal-labelled worked example (1-5) and transferred to a reading-log practice, with an everyday analogy before every defined term and nearly every claim traced to a recorded source. The most important fixes are the answer cues (every keyed option is the longest and 8 of 10 sit at ②, with no shuffling), q9 asking for the 「最初に送る依頼」 against the commit-first step, and the practice model answer that gives no way to enter 「読み終えた日」.
